q-39403.name: Question 1
q-39403.problem: The third and fourth terms of an arithmetic sequence are $-60$ and $-76,$ respectively. Determine the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence.
q-39403.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term is given by 

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d,
$$

so we need to figure out the first term ${a}_{1}$ and the common difference $d.$

Since the terms ${a}_{3}=-60$ and ${a}_{4}=-76$ are consecutive, we can subtract to find the common difference:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{4}-{a}_{3} \\  & =-76-(-60) \\  & =-16\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, ${a}_{3}=-60,$ to determine the first term of the sequence. Since ${a}_{3}$ is $2$ jumps after ${a}_{1},$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{3} & ={a}_{1}+2d \\ -60 & ={a}_{1}+2(-16) \\ -60 & ={a}_{1}-32 \\ -28 & ={a}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

So the formula for the $n$th term of this arithmetic sequence is:  

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =-28+(n-1)(-16) \\  & =-28-16n+16 \\  & =-16n-12\end{aligned}
$$

q-39403.html:
Question 1
?

The third and fourth terms of an arithmetic sequence are −60 and −76, respectively. Determine the formula for the nth term of the sequence.

a
 an=−16n−12
b
 an=−28n−32
c
 an=−28n−2
d
 an=−16n−28
e
 an=−16n−44
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The formula for the nth term is given by

an=a1+(n−1)d,

so we need to figure out the first term a1 and the common difference d.

Since the terms a3=−60 and a4=−76 are consecutive, we can subtract to find the common difference:

d=a4−a3=−76−(−60)=−16

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, a3=−60, to determine the first term of the sequence. Since a3 is 2 jumps after a1, we have:

a3=a1+2d−60=a1+2(−16)−60=a1−32−28=a1

So the formula for the nth term of this arithmetic sequence is:

an=a1+(n−1)d=−28+(n−1)(−16)=−28−16n+16=−16n−12

q-101048.name: Question 2
q-101048.problem: An arithmetic sequence has the $3$rd term ${a}_{3}=-9$ and the $8$th term ${a}_{8}=-19.$  Calculate the $11$th term.
q-101048.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term is given by 

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d,
$$

 

so we need to figure out the first term ${a}_{1}$ and the common difference $d.$

To find the common difference, we can find the total difference between the terms ${a}_{3}=-9$ and ${a}_{8}=-19$ and divide it by the number of jumps, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\frac{{a}_{8}-{a}_{3}}{8-3} \\  & =\frac{-19-(-9)}{8-3} \\  & =\frac{-10}{5} \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, ${a}_{3}=-9,$ to determine the first term of the sequence. Since ${a}_{3}$ is $2$ jumps after ${a}_{1},$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{3} & ={a}_{1}+2d \\ -9 & ={a}_{1}+2(-2) \\ -9 & ={a}_{1}-4 \\ {a}_{1} & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

So, the formula for the $n$th term is:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =-5+(n-1)\cdot (-2) \\  & =-5-2n+2 \\  & =-3-2n\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can find the $11$th term by substituting $n=11$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{11} & =-3-2(11) \\  & =-3-22 \\  & =-25\end{aligned}
$$

q-101048.html:
Question 2
?

An arithmetic sequence has the 3rd term a3=−9 and the 8th term a8=−19. Calculate the 11th term.

a
−25
b
23
c
−27
d
−31
e
34
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The formula for the nth term is given by

an=a1+(n−1)d,

so we need to figure out the first term a1 and the common difference d.

To find the common difference, we can find the total difference between the terms a3=−9 and a8=−19 and divide it by the number of jumps, as follows:

d=a8−a38−3=−19−(−9)8−3=−105=−2

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, a3=−9, to determine the first term of the sequence. Since a3 is 2 jumps after a1, we have:

a3=a1+2d−9=a1+2(−2)−9=a1−4a1=−5

So, the formula for the nth term is:

an=−5+(n−1)⋅(−2)=−5−2n+2=−3−2n

Finally, we can find the 11th term by substituting n=11 into the above:

a11=−3−2(11)=−3−22=−25

q-177693.name: Question 3
q-177693.problem: The $7$th and $8$th terms of an arithmetic sequence are $-39$ and $-31,$ respectively. Determine the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence.
q-177693.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term is given by 

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d,
$$

so we need to figure out the first term ${a}_{1}$ and the common difference $d.$

Since the terms ${a}_{7}=-39$ and ${a}_{8}=-31$ are consecutive, we can subtract them to find the common difference:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{8}-{a}_{7} \\  & =-31-(-39) \\  & =-31+39 \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, ${a}_{7}=-39,$ to determine the first term of the sequence. Since ${a}_{7}$ is $6$ jumps after ${a}_{1},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{7} & ={a}_{1}+6d \\ -39 & ={a}_{1}+6(8) \\ -39 & ={a}_{1}+48 \\ -39-48 & ={a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =-87.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the formula for the $n$th term of this arithmetic sequence is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =-87+(n-1)(8) \\  & =-87+8n-8 \\  & =8n-95.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

The 7th and 8th terms of an arithmetic sequence are −39 and −31, respectively. Determine the formula for the nth term of the sequence.

a
an=8n−87
b
an=7n−88
c
an=6n−81
d
an=7n−80
e
an=8n−95
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The formula for the nth term is given by an=a1+(n−1)d, so we need to figure out the first term a1 and the common difference d.

Since the terms a7=−39 and a8=−31 are consecutive, we can subtract them to find the common difference: d=a8−a7=−31−(−39)=−31+39=8

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, a7=−39, to determine the first term of the sequence. Since a7 is 6 jumps after a1, we have a7=a1+6d−39=a1+6(8)−39=a1+48−39−48=a1a1=−87.

So, the formula for the nth term of this arithmetic sequence is an=a1+(n−1)d=−87+(n−1)(8)=−87+8n−8=8n−95.
